If $\beta=\pm 1$ and $\nu$ is a $(\beta,\sigma)$ -admissible shape then $S(\mathfrak{c}_{n}(\sigma))$ admits an involutive Poisson automorphism

(5.25)

$\displaystyle\tau:e_{a,i,b,j}t^{r}\mapsto(\beta)^{i+j}(-1)^{r-1+s(\nu)_{a,b}}e_{b,j^{\prime},a,i^{\prime}}t^{r}.$

The Dirac reduction $R(S(\mathfrak{c}_{n}(\sigma),\tau)=S(\mathfrak{c}_{n}(\sigma)^{\tau})$ is Poisson generated by

$\displaystyle\begin{array}[]{l}\{\eta_{a,i,j;r}\mid 1\leq a\leq m,\ 1\leq i,j\leq\nu_{a},\ r\geq 0\}\\
\hskip 40.0pt\cup\{\theta_{a,i,j;r}\mid 1\leq a\leq m-1,\ 1\leq i\leq\nu_{a},\ 1\leq j\leq\nu_{a+1},\ r\geq s_{a,a+1}\}\end{array}$

subject to the relations

(5.28)

$\displaystyle\eta_{a,i,j,r}=(\beta)^{i+j}(-1)^{r-1}\eta_{a,j^{\prime},i^{\prime},r}$

(5.29)

$\displaystyle\left\{\eta_{a,i,j;r},\eta_{b,h,k;s}\right\}=\delta_{a,b}\frac{1}{2}(\delta_{h,j}\eta_{a,i,k;r+s}-\delta_{i,k}\eta_{a,h,j;r+s}+(\beta)^{h+k}(-1)^{s-1}(\eta_{a,i,h^{\prime};r+s}\delta_{k^{\prime},j}-\delta_{i,h^{\prime}}\eta_{a,k^{\prime},j;r+s}))$

(5.30)

$\displaystyle\left\{\eta_{a,i,j;r},\theta_{b,h,k;s}\right\}$
$\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}(\delta_{a,b}\delta_{h,j}\theta_{a,i,k;r+s}-\delta_{a,b+1}\delta_{i,k}\theta_{b,h,j;r+s})$

(5.31)

$\displaystyle+(\beta)^{i+j}\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{r-1}(\delta_{a,b}\delta_{h,i^{\prime}}\theta_{a,j^{\prime},k;r+s}-\delta_{a,b+1}\delta_{k^{\prime},j}\theta_{b,h,i^{\prime};r+s})$

(5.32)

$\{\theta_{a,i,j;r},\theta_{a,h,k;s}\}=\frac{1}{2}(\beta)^{h+k}(-1)^{s_{a,a+1}+s-1}(\delta_{i,h^{\prime}}\eta_{a+1,k^{\prime},j;r+s}-\delta_{k,j^{\prime}}\eta_{a,i,h^{\prime},r+s}) for r

(5.33)

$\displaystyle\{\theta_{a,i,j;r},\theta_{a+1,h,k;s}\}-\{\theta_{a,i,j;r+1},\theta_{a+1,h,k;s}\}=0$

(5.34)

$\displaystyle\{\theta_{a,i,j;r},\theta_{b,h,k;s}\}=0\textnormal{ for }b>a+1\textnormal{ or if }b=a+1\textnormal{ and }h\neq j$

(5.35)

$\displaystyle\{\theta_{a,i,j;r},\{\theta_{a,h,k;s},\theta_{b,f,g;t}\}\}+\{\theta_{a,i,j;s},\{\theta_{a,h,k;r},\theta_{b,f,g;t}\}\}=0\textnormal{ if }\mid a-b\mid=1\textnormal{ and }r+s\textnormal{ odd}$

$\displaystyle\begin{array}[]{l}\{\theta_{a,i,j;r},\{\theta_{a,h,k;s},\theta_{b,f,g;t}\}\}+\{\theta_{a,i,j;s},\{\theta_{a,h,k;r},\theta_{b,f,g;t}\}\}\\
\hskip 80.0pt=\frac{1}{2}(\beta)^{i+j}(-1)^{r+s_{a,a+1}}\left(\delta_{a+1,b}\delta_{f,k}\delta_{h,i^{\prime}}\theta_{a+1,j^{\prime},g;r+s+t}+\delta_{a,b+1}\delta_{h,g}\delta_{j^{\prime},k}\theta_{b,f,i^{\prime};r+s+t}\right)\\
\hskip 120.0pt\textnormal{ if }\mid a-b\mid=1\textnormal{ and }r+s\textnormal{ even}.\end{array}$
card.label: Theorem 5.3

paper.title: Shifted twisted Yangians and Slodowy slices in classical Lie algebras
paper.abstract: In this paper we introduce the shifted twisted Yangian of type {\sf AI}, following the work of Lu--Wang--Zhang, and we study their semiclassical limits, a class of Poisson algebras. We demonstrate that they coincide with the Dirac reductions of the semiclassical shifted Yangian for $\mathfrak{gl}_n$. We deduce that these shifted twisted Yangians admit truncations which are isomorphic to Slodowy slices for many non-rectangular nilpotent elements in types {\sf B}, {\sf C}, {\sf D}. As a direct consequence we obtain parabolic presentations of the semiclassical shifted twisted Yangian, analogous to those introduced by Brundan--Kleshchev for the Yangian of type {\sf A}. Finally we give Poisson presentations of Slodowy slices for all even nilpotent elements in types {\sf B}, {\sf C}, {\sf D}, generalising the recent work of the second author.
